items.title: Sumner Labat Interview, 1962-11-11
items.q: And they had Manuel Alexander, he was the drummer. ... I was leading the orchestra, you see.

ctx.x: Sure. The Supreme Band that was here? Yeah. That's right. Who was the members of it? Do you remember? Yes.

Every one of them did except me. Really? We had about seven of us. Who was the members of it? There was Armand Tweedo. What did he play? He played trombone. There was Babe Bennett. He played cornet. Paul Maurice played clarinet. I played the violin at that time. I was leading the orchestra, you see. And they had Manuel Alexander, he was the drummer. That's it? And Dota frozen boy, he played guitar. And Edward Anderson, he played the bass violin. That was the lineup we had. Yeah. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm.…
Did Paul Maurice play any other instruments?

items.title: Sumner Labat Interview, 1962-11-11
items.q: One Saturday he came over here to play with my band, with me

ctx.x: Other part is all right but he didn't die.

I saw him at the bank with a couple of months or a meeting. Yeah. That Miles there we was trying to figure out what was Tess's name and I couldn't think of him. I knew him. At the same time I was talking about Tiddy Tat, the puzzle of the letter. But I knew I thought about Alexander's name. Yeah, that's his name. He's not Alexander's name. He's not Alexander's name. He's not Alexander's name. He's not Alexander's name. I remember where he is.

One Saturday he came over here to play with my band, with me and we had meatballs and spaghetti for dinner. Tex got drunk and left out there with a spaghetti sandwich. I knew I was trying to go out there. That was one of my biggest spaghetti sandwich in my life. That's a new one on me.
